bullets.text: Wildfires continue to devastate parts of Europe, with a blaze near Bordeaux, France, tearing through over 162 square miles in less than four days, leading to concerns about further evacuations.
Uganda has initiated emergency food handouts after 19 people died from hunger, following months of drought and crop failures that have left 1.5 million people facing malnutrition.
Shots were fired near the US consulate in Toronto for the second time this year; no one was injured, and police engaged in a high-speed chase but failed to apprehend the suspect.
The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion is ongoing in Sydney, focusing on education and training improvements to prevent hate.
Victoria Premier Jacinta Allan is facing a leadership challenge, with Ben Carroll nominating himself ahead of a Labor caucus meeting.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has praised Sally McManus and Michele O’Neil as "giants" following their surprise announcement to step down from the ACTU.
Investors are increasingly concerned about the rising credit risks for Big Tech companies due to a surge in borrowing to fund massive investments in data centers for AI development.
Oil prices tumbled significantly after the US paused daily strikes against Iran and tankers resumed loading at a Kazakh export terminal, easing supply pressures in the market.
JPMorgan Chase & Co. analysts indicated that an in-house indicator is now flashing a "buy-signal" for the S&P 500 Index, suggesting a potential rally.
